builtFrom.catalog: code read through the repo's Atlas map when it has one, else the plan's code scope; described with Foundry's catalog describer prompts
builtFrom.method: three independent model proposals, item-level majority vote (2 of 3), seams to the size ceiling, per-region authoring

concepts.description: Writing what an action means: the ActionRule algebra (string delegation, { rel, action } walks, { rule } json-rules conditions, any/all, boolean, null), a RebacSchema with the app's own action names, per-record permissionRules that only widen
Keeping rules positive and acyclic: validateActionRule, validateSchema, schemaRuleIssues; a check throws on a schema holding any refused rule
Rules about who is acting: permix.setActor({ model, record }) read by plain { rule } conditions under __actor, acting on your own row via { rel: 'user' }, person-only rules and null-actor pitfalls
Cross-source rel walks: schema bridges (json-rules Bridge), map:model segments, far rows passed as subject.data, an absent far row denies

Deciding allow/deny on one hydrated record: createRebacCheck(map) and check(permix, schema, subject, action), walk order (superadmin, table, schema OR row rule, entitlements), cycle detection, permissions.idField, exact strings
Explaining or charging a use: createRebacPaths returns every admission as chains of entitlement refs, limit and PathLimitError
The SchemaMap every walk, placement and hydrator reads: resources to models, the json-rules/prisma-map fieldMap, the false-polymorphism registry, to-one FK-owning relations
Loading the record a check walks: createHydrator({ map, load }) follows to-one relations recursively through the app's load, /// @permissions(hydrate: false) skips an edge
What a check costs by walk depth and entitlements held; bun run bench and *.bench.ts
What the actor holds: createPermissions, the grant table, entitlements, superadmin flag and actor, setup(entries, { owner?, replace? }), getJSON, PermixLike

Access anchored on a record and backed by its owner: EntitlementEntry (anchor with path, positive where, actions, ref), polymorphic steps, live owner re-walk, reachableFrom, entitlementProblem, coversEntitlement, withoutRedundantEntitlements
Whether a writer may grant an entitlement: createCanGrantEntitlement's two passes, placeEntitlement/placeUnder pseudo records, delegatedWhere narrowing, held entitlements never combine
Tokens and integrations acting for an owner: delegate (full / ceiling / entitlements), capAtRole, Permissions as data, installPermissions, permixOf, wellFormedEntitlements
Modelling tenants: membership (acting as the tenant) versus entitlements the tenant owns (licensing), and what keeps a boundary closed
What the package is and its vocabulary: one synchronous check over the app's own records covering RBAC, ReBAC, ABAC and delegation, rules as data, no second store
Where code belongs: src/core never imports src/helpers (test/layout.test.ts), fetching and role mapping stay in the app
Use this or another system: comparison with SpiceDB, OpenFGA, Permify, Cedar, Oso, Cerbos, Casbin, CASL, OPA; no tuple store, positive rules only, live delegation, where others are ahead
Not built yet: the 1.0 reflection (rules to Prisma where / SQL, listing, reverse lookup); today a check judges one loaded record
